title: A New Interpretation of Information Rate
summary: Original Kelly paper: maximizing expected log wealth maximizes long-run growth; for an even-money bet with win probability p, bet 2p - 1.

title: The Kelly Criterion in Blackjack, Sports Betting, and the Stock Market
summary: Practitioner Kelly formulas: f* = (m - r)/s^2 (2.2x for the S&P 500 at r = 6%, 1.33x if borrowing costs 8%), fractional Kelly c gives c(2-c) of max growth and P(ever halving) = 0.5^(2/c-1).

title: Good and bad properties of the Kelly criterion
authors: L. MacLean, E. Thorp, W. Ziemba
summary: Lists Kelly's good (max asymptotic growth, no ruin) and bad (huge bets, rough short-run paths, 700 bets with 14% edge can turn $1000 into $18) properties; argues for fractional Kelly.

title: Rational Decision-Making Under Uncertainty: Observed Betting Patterns on a Biased Coin
summary: 61 finance-trained subjects with a 60% coin and $25: 28% went bust, 21% hit the $250 cap, average payout $91; Kelly (20% per flip) was almost unknown and martingale beliefs common.

title: Optimal leverage from non-ergodicity
summary: Time-average growth of a leveraged GBM investment has a unique optimal leverage (mu - r)/sigma^2, while ensemble-average returns rise linearly with leverage and invite overleverage; the Sharpe ratio is leverage-invariant.

title: Leverage efficiency
summary: Hypothesis that markets drive the market portfolio's optimal leverage to 1; S&P 500 1927-2020 l_opt = 1.1 (s.e. 0.6), Bitcoin 1.5 (0.3), both about 1.0 after costs; Madoff's fake returns imply 100-300.

title: George Costanza at It Again: The Leveraged ETF Episode
summary: Daily-reset leverage suffers volatility drag, static leverage risks wipeout; over 1927-2020 about 1.5x leverage ended with the most money and a Merton investor (risk aversion 2.5) would hold about 85% equities.

title: Path-Dependence of Leveraged ETF Returns
summary: Exact formula: L-times daily-reset fund log return = L x index log return - (L^2 - L)/2 x realized variance - costs; confirmed on 56 US LETFs from 2008; unsuitable for buy-and-hold without rebalancing.

title: Leverage for the Long Run: A Systematic Approach to Managing Risk and Magnifying Returns in Stocks
summary: S&P 500 1928-2015: hold 1.25/2/3x above the 200-day SMA, T-bills below; Sharpe 0.53/0.51/0.47 vs 0.30 buy-and-hold, max drawdown -59/-79/-92% vs -86%, with an optimistic 1% annual leverage cost.

title: Leveraging the U.S. Stock Market Based on SMA Rules (review of Gayed & Bilello)
summary: Critical review: the 1% leverage cost and ignored switching costs overstate results and the 1928 start flatters SMA rules; 2x LRS Sharpe 0.51 (-78%) vs 0.30 (-86%).

title: Hedgefundie's Excellent Adventure: a 3x leveraged ETF portfolio
summary: HFEA (55% UPRO / 45% TMF, quarterly rebalance, 165/135 effective exposure) was down about 53% by October 2022 when bonds failed as a hedge; snapshot also records TQQQ's -81.7% 2021-22 drawdown vs QQQ -32.7%.

title: Hacker News threads: Kelly Criterion; 3x leveraged ETFs; Towards a new leveraged ETF
summary: Practitioner comments: half Kelly as common practice, Kelly in HFT sizing, LETFs as covert short-volatility instruments, path dependence of daily reset.

title: Diversification Across Time
summary: Lifecycle investing: up to 2:1 leverage when young, de-lever with age; since 1871 it matches a 75% stock mean with 21% lower standard deviation and a 37% certainty-equivalent gain (CRRA 4).

title: Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity
authors: C. Asness, A. Frazzini, L. Pedersen
summary: Leverage-averse investors overpay for risky assets, so levered safe assets win: risk parity Sharpe 0.52-0.53 vs 0.25 market and 0.40 60/40 (1926-2010), 0.61 vs 0.43 (1973-2010).

title: Betting Against Beta
summary: Funding-constraint model; long levered low-beta, short high-beta earns a US Sharpe of 0.75 (1926-2009) and works across 20 countries, bonds and futures.

title: Betting against betting against beta
summary: BAB's performance comes from non-standard construction that effectively equal-weights micro caps (about $1.05 per $1 in the bottom 1% by size); net returns are explained by profitability and investment tilts.

title: What is return stacking? / Return Stacking: Strategies for Overcoming a Low Return Environment
authors: C. Hoffstein, R. Gordillo et al. (Return Stacked)
summary: Portable-alpha style leverage: $1 of core beta via futures plus $1 of an uncorrelated strategy per $1 invested; risks are stacked losses, financing cost and correlations rising in crises.

title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
summary: Scaling exposure by inverse past-month variance earns a 4.9% alpha and a 25% higher Sharpe on the US market (weights median ~1, 99th percentile 6.4x); works across equity factors and FX carry.

title: The Impact of Volatility Targeting
authors: C. Harvey, E. Hoyle, R. Korgaonkar, S. Rattray, M. Sargaison, O. Van Hemert
summary: Across 60+ assets since 1926, volatility targeting raises Sharpe only for risk assets with a leverage effect (US equities 0.40 to 0.48-0.51) and thins left tails everywhere; no Sharpe gain for bonds, FX, commodities.

title: On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios
authors: S. Cederburg, M. O'Doherty, F. Wang, X. Yan
summary: Across 103 equity strategies volatility-managed versions do not systematically outperform (45 better, 58 worse); real-time combinations earn lower certainty-equivalent returns in 72 of 103 cases.

title: ESMA agrees to prohibit binary options and restrict CFDs to protect retail investors
summary: 74-89% of retail CFD accounts lose money (average loss EUR 1,600-29,000); caps of 30:1 major FX, 20:1 gold and major indices, 10:1 commodities, 5:1 shares, 2:1 crypto; 50% margin close-out.

title: FCA proposes stricter rules for contract for difference products (CP16/40)
summary: 82% of a representative sample of UK retail CFD clients lost money while leverage over 200:1 was on offer; proposed 50:1 cap (25:1 for inexperienced clients).

title: Traders' performance will improve under new ESMA leverage limits, finds research from Capital.com
summary: Capital.com internal data: lower leverage cut users margin-called within 15 days from about 30% to 5% and the average loss by over 80%; current risk warning says 79.75% of retail accounts lose money.

title: Should Retail Investors' Leverage Be Limited?
summary: The 2010 US 50:1 retail FX cap cut volume 23% and high-leverage traders' losses 40%; before it the top leverage quintile lost 44% a month vs 3% for the bottom; spreads unchanged.

title: The leverage substitution
summary: ESMA's 2018 CFD cap cut treated traders' leverage from 6.6 to 4.7 and large losses, but they shifted to more volatile stocks and crypto, partly substituting risk for leverage.

title: Leverage Is a Double-Edged Sword
authors: A. Subrahmanyam, K. Tang, J. Wang, X. Yang
summary: Chinese futures traders: one more unit of leverage costs about 5.3 bp a day, via trading costs and margin-call liquidations (most of unskilled traders' losses); skilled traders gain from leverage.

title: Liquidation, Leverage and Optimal Margin in Bitcoin Futures Markets
authors: Z. Cheng, J. Deng, T. Wang, M. Yu
summary: BitMEX perpetuals: daily forced liquidations 3.51% (long) and 1.89% (short) of open interest, liquidated traders averaged 60x, and a 1% daily margin-call probability needs 3x (long) / 5x (short) leverage limits.

title: The Leverage Cycle
summary: Equilibrium sets leverage (margins) as well as interest rates; leverage rises in calm booms and collapses in crises, amplifying price swings, so it should be regulated.

title: Carry Trades and Currency Crashes
authors: M. Brunnermeier, S. Nagel, L. Pedersen
summary: Leveraged currency carry trades have negatively skewed returns and crash when risk appetite and funding liquidity fall and carry positions unwind together.

title: Improving on bold play when the gambler is restricted
summary: States Dubins and Savage's theorem that bold play (stake min(fortune, goal - fortune)) maximizes the chance of reaching a goal in a subfair game, and shows it is not optimal when the stake per bet is capped.

title: Theory of constant proportion portfolio insurance
summary: CPPI: risky exposure = multiplier x (wealth - floor), a constant leverage on the cushion that adds exposure after gains and protects a floor except against gaps larger than 1/multiplier.

title: Arena leverage statistics from our 1-minute candles, 2024-01 to 2026-09
summary: Our own numbers: volatility, funding, in-sample Kelly and l_opt per instrument, margin-call hit rates by tier, the Sharpe ratio each tier would need under Kelly, and volatility-drag tables.
